mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a potential for continued accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising employment (PAYEMS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases over 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a single month, coupled with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic pessimism spreads.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook improve.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where GDP increases over two consecutive quarters.
